newsitem.title: POLAND: Bill on Polish BGZ bank to allow EBRD purchase.
newsitem.headline: Bill on Polish BGZ bank to allow EBRD purchase.

text.p: Polish Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA (BGZ) is working on a plan, which would allow the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to buy a BGZ stake, a senior BGZ official said on Friday.

The plan, to be ready by April, will pave the way for the government to amend a bill on BGZ so that it could embrace shareholders other than cooperative banks, which is required by the current law, the head of BGZ's board Antoni Magdon said.
"The strategic plan for the (BGZ) group will be ready by April... It will amend the 1994 bill...in order to build a partnership with EBRD and the entry of its capital," he told Reuters.

Magdon said that BGZ, which is the so-called national bank for the country's 1,200 cooperative banks grouped in nine regional banks, picked Deliotte & Touche last week to advise the bank in creating the new bill.
The treasury, which holds 66 percent of BGZ, said last year that it was in negotiations to sell 14 percent of the farming bank to EBRD.
BGZ's gross profit in 1996 rose 37.1 percent to 495.4 million zlotys. Its capital eased 6.3 percent to 1.502 billion zlotys and its gross balance sheet rose 20 percent to 13.952 billion zlotys.
